## Done — image is ready

**`/work/SystemContext.svg`** (2.8 KB, valid SVG)

Your `workspace.dsl` defines exactly **one view** (`systemContext library "SystemContext"`), so there's one image file. It renders the C4 System Context diagram:

- **Patron** — Person (stick figure, navy)
- **Library** — Software System (blue)
- **Patron → Library** — "Browses the catalogue through" `[HTTPS]`
- Plus a title and a small legend.

Open it in any browser or SVG viewer.

### One important note on how I produced it
This environment has **no local renderer** (no PlantUML/Java/Python/Node/Graphviz/Inkscape), **no root** to install one, and **no public internet** (DNS for `plantuml.com` and the apk mirror both fail — only the internal LLM + Structurizr-MCP hosts resolve). The Structurizr MCP server can only export to *text* (PlantUML/Mermaid), not images.

So rather than a PlantUML/Structurizr raster, I **generated the SVG directly from the parsed model** (I validated the workspace and pulled the exact elements/relationships from the export). It's a faithful, standard C4-style rendering of the view — just hand-authored instead of tool-rendered.

If you'd prefer the exact PlantUML output, I can also drop the generated `.puml` source file(s) into the directory so you can render them wherever a PlantUML toolchain exists. Want me to add those?
